thread.title: In Smartwatch Market, It’s The Apple Watch Vs. The Also-Rans

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: In Smartwatch Market, It’s The Apple Watch Vs. The Also-Rans
text:
Just as the iPod came to dominate the portable music player market, the Apple Watch has assumed a similar overwhelming lead in the nascent smartwatch market.
X Apple 's ( AAPL ) smartwatch leads by a mile in the wrist-worn wearable device game, even when counting basic fitness trackers from other companies. It controls nearly five times the market share of its nearest rival.
Not bad for getting off to a slow start when it launched in April 2015 with a huge variety of models. They ranged from a basic sports model costing $349 on up to a luxury gold model starting at $10,000.
Critics knocked the first-generation device for its lack of a killer app and the fact that it needed to be paired with an iPhone for full functionality. Early on, the main function of the device was for "glanceable" notifications. For instance, the Apple Watch can alert you to text messages you might otherwise have missed if your phone was tucked away in your pocket.

Fourth-Generation Apple Watch Coming Soon "It's still a work in progress for Apple," IDC analyst Ramon Llamas told Investor's Business Daily. "They are really taking their time introducing feature sets."
Last September, Apple added the most-desired feature: built-in cellular wireless. That allows users to leave their iPhones at home when they exercise.
With built-in cellular, Apple Watch Series 3 users can make and receive phone calls and text messages on their wrist.
Next month, analysts expect Apple to introduce its fourth-generation smartwatch. The Apple Watch Series 4 is rumored to feature 15% larger displays and enhanced heart-rate detection.
More Than Half Of All Sales Last year, Apple accounted for 53.1% of global smartwatch sales, research firm IDC said. Samsung was a distant second at 10.9%.
In the first quarter, the most recent period for which IDC has data, Apple Watch grabbed 47.1% of the smartwatch market, followed by Samsung with 9.9%. Trailing even further behind were companies like Garmin ( GRMN ) and Fitbit ( FIT ).
Apple doesn't disclose its watch sales, but IDC estimates it has sold 44.6 million units in its first three years of availability. That's 55% of all smartwatches sold during that period.
In the June quarter, Apple said its watch sales grew in the mid-40% range year over year.
Three Reasons For Apple Watch Success Apple has been successful in the market for three main reasons, Llamas said. First, Apple has strong brand loyalty with consumers. Second, it didn't cram the watch with too many features that might confuse buyers. Third, it has developed a niche for the watch in its broader product ecosystem.
The Apple Watch has become a natural extension of the iPhone, Llamas said. Apple Watch users can access the Siri voice assistant and make Apple Pay mobile payments with the wearable device. The watch can even stream the company's Apple Music service.
The market is still young for smartwatches, Llamas said. Last year, smartwatch sales totaled 33.3 million units worldwide. This year, they are expected to reach 43.5 million, an increase of 31%. IDC forecasts smartwatch sales to climb to 89 million units in 2022.
In the future, they might become more integrated into the health care industry. They could even play a role in location-based advertising and marketing, Llamas said.
"Smartwatches are still a solution in search of a problem," he said.
